answer: When k identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, the protocol detects their shared behavior and scales penalties with the number of identity pairs, yielding O(k²) slashing against bonded escrows. A sybil operator therefore cannot treat each key as an independent, cheap risk: on detection, asymmetric capital depreciation applies an exponential multiplier to aggregate loss. Like a grove or orchard fed through one inlet, apparently separate branches may expose a common source.
